content: 1. Aspirin enhances the effects of insulin glargine through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may increase the risk of hypoglycemia, particularly when insulin is co-administered with high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day). Adjustments to the insulin dose and more frequent glucose monitoring may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Aspirin increases the effects of insulin glulisine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration with high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may elevate the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and increased glucose monitoring frequency may be required. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 3. Aspirin enhances the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic synergy. High doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and frequent glucose monitoring may be necessary. Close monitoring is essential. 4. Aspirin increases the effects of insulin isophane human and insulin regular human via pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration with high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may heighten the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and more frequent glucose monitoring may be required. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 5. Aspirin enhances the effects of insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic synergy. High doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and frequent glucose monitoring may be necessary. Close monitoring is advised. 6. Aspirin increases the effects of insulin lispro protamine/insulin lispro via pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration with high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may elevate the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and increased glucose monitoring frequency may be required. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 7. Aspirin enhances the effects of insulin NPH through pharmacodynamic synergy. High doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and frequent glucose monitoring may be necessary. Close monitoring is essential. 8. Aspirin increases the effects of insulin regular human via pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration with high doses of salicylates (≥3 g/day) may heighten the risk of hypoglycemia. Insulin dose adjustments and more frequent glucose monitoring may be required. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Aspirin and irbesartan may increase each other's toxicity through an unspecified mechanism. Aspirin reduces the effects of irbesartan via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs can increase serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 10. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while isoproterenol decreases them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Aspirin and ketoprofen both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin may increase ketoprofen levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 12. Aspirin and ketorolac both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. The combination may result in significant toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Alternative therapies should be considered. Aspirin may also increase ketorolac levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Aspirin decreases the levels of L-methylfolate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 14. Aspirin reduces the effects of labetalol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use may diminish the antihypertensive effects of labetalol. Both drugs can increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Aspirin decreases the levels of larotrectinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 16. Aspirin and latanoprost have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Conflicting reports suggest that co-administration of NSAIDs with ophthalmic prostaglandins may either increase or decrease intraocular pressure (IOP). Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Aspirin reduces the efficacy of lesinurad at doses >325 mg/day. However, doses ≤325 mg/day (e.g., for cardiovascular prophylaxis) do not affect lesinurad efficacy and can be co-administered. Close monitoring is recommended. 18. Aspirin increases serum potassium levels, while levalbuterol decreases them. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Aspirin decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 20. Aspirin and levomilnacipran may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. SNRIs like levomilnacipran may further impair platelet activity in patients taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs. Caution and close monitoring are advised.
